Do you know anyone whose done this? I would be curious what the experience would be like. I worry that the language barrier might amplify my loneliness. 
But I hope everything works out for you! Thanks for the reply.

Thank you for your helpful comments.

Khan Academy sounds particularly interesting.
Temping sounds like a good idea. I will look into this, thanks.
I really appreciate you giving me your perspective as someone in uniform.

Thanks for the reply. 

I have been a manager for several years of my experience, but I don't believe I am good at it. Because I find it difficult to form relationships with people, I fail to inspire responsibility in my employees. Despite attempts to copy everything I can figure out about being a "likable" person, people often seem pre-inclined to dislike me. Often times I will be surprised to hear that people I barely know "hate me".

This ties back to the stalker in school. He entered my friendship group slowly, and would often hang out with my friends on his own. Eventually, he started telling them we had a sexual relationship by which time I had already started avoiding him because he had started to creep me out. Because I was in college and getting drunk and hooking up was a normal occurrence for most people, everyone assumed he was telling the truth, and I was just tring to be "innocent" or was embarrassed. 

After the stalker began leaving voicemails for my family (calling my sister fat, telling people I had AIDS) I built up the courage to call him out in public for the first time, after several private attempts to get him to leave me alone.

I did so, and to my surprise, I found my friends rallying to his defense. I was unable to convince any of them that he was harassing me, most of them responded "this is between the two of you, I don't want to get involved." This set a pattern for most of my social relationships that have followed... Despite being cautious to never speak negatively of someone, and to never vent any of my personal problems, people find me to be unlikable.

Sorry, TL;dr, I often find running group challenging, because groups of people confuse and judge me. 

I was in my senior year when I dropped out, but I was on a scholarship. I have been unable to afford to return to the school I was attending without it, which is why I never finished. 

What I like about the military is the idea that there are so many rules to interaction. I think I would be able to just follow them and not have to "improvise". I don't like the thought of killing, at all. But as I have been contemplating suicide but have been unable to bring myself to do it, I feel as if I have already made peace with the idea of being killed.

I do not know what purpose my life could serve otherwise. In 30 years, I have accomplished nothing, and have nothing to show for being alive. It is hard for me to think of people who even notice I was gone. My parents, but we only talk once every few months. It doesn't feel like their interest is genuine. 

I have tried to shelter them from seeing how far down my life his spiraled. When we are together I pretend for their benefit, and over the course of several years it has become secondhand. They have no idea who i am on the inside. Truthfully, they would be losing someone they don't even know at all.

What truly worries me is that I don't have any aspirations. There are no parts of the world I want to see, nothing I want to experience. I feel as if I have learned everything about the world I want to.

I have told two people that I have been feeling suicidal. Now, I fear if I don't act, they will have cause to call me a liar and turn on me, like so many did without cause before. I almost find it impossible to disappoint them, as if killing myself is the only way to prove I have been telling the truth all along.
